Bacterial_Leaf_Streak_Black_Chaff.quote: Bacterial streak appears first as small water-soaked lesions that rapidly develop into long, thin, tan-brown, water-soaked lesions, confined between the leaf veins.
Symptoms include purplish-black longitudinal stripes on glumes that can also be seen on the peduncle and the rachis.

Barley_Yellow_Dwarf_Virus.quote: Barley yellow dwarf symptoms include yellow, red, and/or purple discoloration of leaves.
primary symptoms of Barley Yellow Dwarf virus include plant stunting, reduced tillering, and yellowing and purpling of tips and margins of upper leaves.

Head_Scab.quote: Symptoms of FHB include bleached spikelets and small, shrunken kernels.
The fungus may infect the stem immediately below the head (peduncle), causing a brown to purplish discoloration of the stem tissue.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: Powdery white, gray, or buff-color spore masses develop on leaves, stems, and heads.

Powdery mildew is characterized by white, cottony patches (colonies) of mycelium and conidia on the surface of the plant, occurring on all aerial parts including stems and heads, but most conspicuous on the upper surfaces of lower leaves.

Root_Rot.quote: Symptoms include dark, chocolate brown to black lesions on the coleoptile, stem, roots, and/or subcrown internode (the area above the seed to the soil line).
Heavily diseased roots result in stunting and poor tiller and root development.

Rust.quote: Stem rust occurs primarily on stems but can also be found on leaves, sheaths, glumes, awns, and even seed.
Reddish-brown, oval to elongated pustules break out of stems, leaf sheaths, leaves and occasionally on inflorescences.

Septoria_Leaf_Blotch.quote: Initial symptoms of Septoria tritici blotch develop on the lower leaves as chlorotic flecks and expand into irregular brown lesions.

Wheat_Streak_Mosaic_Virus.quote: The major symptoms of wheat streak mosaic are stunted plants with mottled and streaked leaves, with light green and dark-green or yellow and green mosaics that coalesce into streaks being characteristic of this disease.
Typically, infected plants are stunted, may be splayed on the ground, and do not tiller as well as unaffected plants.
